CANONICAL_NAME.value: LAPACK (reference) -- the blocked successor that superseded LINPACK and EISPACK

value.lineage: LAPACK (Anderson et al., 1992-) rewrote the LINPACK/EISPACK functionality around BLOCKED algorithms expressed in Level-3 BLAS (matrix-matrix), so that data loaded into cache is reused O(block) times. It is the WINNER of this pair: same mathematics, different memory-access structure. Kept here as the rival, so the loser can be compared on a shared problem without Techne deciding why it won.

HUMAN_PROBLEM.value: high-performance dense linear algebra on cache-based machines

value.built_to: provide LINPACK/EISPACK functionality at high performance on machines with memory hierarchies, by blocking the algorithms onto Level-3 BLAS
value.pressure: the same O(n^3) arithmetic, but on machines where memory bandwidth, not flops, is the binding constraint
value.success_means: the same numerical answer at a large multiple of the unblocked rate

value.pressure: memory hierarchy: data movement costs more than arithmetic
value.failure_condition: with a badly chosen block size or an unoptimised BLAS it degenerates toward the unblocked rate
